thread:
Maria Gomez: heads-up — customer reported tokens counted incorrectly on streaming disconnects. Per-org burst cap hit, but the API key counters looked fine.
Kevin Liu: seeing that in logs too. sample: 
```
[stream] conn=hd-12f drop=io.timeout tokens_emitted=42 partial_buffer=13 org_id=org_789 key=key_abcd
ratelimit: per_org_remaining=0 per_key_remaining=120
```
Maria Gomez: exact. they got a 429 from the org quota even though their key had credits. Suspect we're double-accounting partial tokens on disconnect + on reconnect.
Jordan Patel: +1. Also noticed reconnect spikes where the client retries and we re-charge already-emitted partial tokens.
Ria Shah: quick question — are we charging for bytes sent vs tokens produced? we have mixed sources in the pipeline (tokenizer + streaming encoder).
Kevin Liu: we charge based on server-side token emit events. problem: when stream breaks mid-token we currently flush X bytes and immediately increment token counters, then on resume we may re-emit the remainder (counts again).
Ops-bot: rate_limit_event: org=org_789 type=burst_exceeded ts=1749534001
SRE-bot: note: this came up in the last postmortem as "partial-charge" pattern.
Maria Gomez: proposal A: adopt a commit-on-ack model — only count tokens when the delivery ACK is confirmed or the connection is closed gracefully. On abrupt disconnects, keep partial buffer reserved for a short grace window (~30s) and only commit on resume or expiration.
Jordan Patel: proposal B: emit a stream-resume token in the protocol. client includes resume_id on reconnect; server reconciles and only charges delta tokens since last-committed offset. This needs client changes but is precise.
Ria Shah: UX/console implications: we should show a "streaming_pending_tokens" metric per-org and per-key so ops can see reserved vs charged. Also a "reconnect_double_charge" alert on abnormal growth.
Kevin Liu: implementation complexity: A is simpler server-side (reserve counters), risk: if clients never reconnect we need to release reservations and maybe credit back. B needs protocol and SDK updates. We can do A as an immediate mitigation behind a feature flag, B as long-term.
Maria Gomez: billing consideration: we must avoid charging customers retroactively. Any backlog of mis-charges should be auto-refunded once we flip the flag. finance ok with a short credit window.
Jordan Patel: streaming rate-limiter behaviour: currently limiting is per-org token rate with burst window. For streaming we should split enforcement: a) per-connection in-flight token budget (soft limit) b) per-org burst budget. That prevents a noisy reconnect loop from draining org budget.
Kevin Liu: agree. practical: add a per-connection "inflight_quota" that decreases as we emit but is not immediately applied to per-org until commit point; however we must expose this in metrics for debugging.
Ria Shah: console change request: in Quotas -> add "Streaming" tab showing: current inflight per-conn, pending reservations, recent disconnects, and a heatmap of per-org bursts. Also add an ability to toggle "strict immediate billing" vs "commit-on-ack" for enterprise customers.
Maria Gomez: rollout plan: ship A behind ff_stream_commit (default off). Canary to 5% orgs, monitor reconnect_double_charge metric and customer support tickets. If stable after 48h, ramp to 50% then 100% next week.
Kevin Liu: telemetry to add before canary: metric stream.partial_charges_count, stream.resume_success_rate, stream.reservation_release_count, and audit logs linking reservation_id -> billing_charge_id.
Jordan Patel: edge-case: clients that NAT/conn-change will open a new TCP with different connection_id. For resume tokens we need a TTL and mapping keyed by org+resume_id. Also guard against resume_id brute-force.
Ria Shah: security: require resume tokens to be HMAC-signed with key secret so only valid clients can resume. admin console should allow revoking resume tokens for a session.
Maria Gomez: decision: implement A (reserve + commit on ack) behind feature flag, add metrics, build refund automation for known mis-charges; start RFC for B (protocol resume token) as next quarter work.
Kevin Liu: creating PR for server changes now (WIP). will include tests for race conditions: disconnect during token flush, reconnect with overlapping chunks, and abort-release flow.
Jordan Patel: I'll add console mockups to the product ticket and wire up the dashboard panels for streaming.
Ria Shah: ops: schedule canary deploy and add an on-call playbook: if we see >0.5% reconnect_double_charge in 1h, flip flag off and run refund script.
Maria Gomez: thanks all. follow-up meeting tomorrow 11am to review PR + new metrics. @Ria please add the panels to the Quotas roadmap doc. :thumbsup:
